items.title: IASB adds cryptoasset and IFRS 16 projects to its work plan
items.summary: At its November meeting the IASB started a narrow-scope project on cryptocurrencies and stablecoins and another on targeted improvements to IFRS 16 Leases. It also set the IFRS 17 post-implementation review for early 2027.
detail: The cryptoasset project will look at measuring cryptocurrencies at fair value through profit or loss, and at whether some stablecoins could qualify as cash equivalents under IAS 7.

The IFRS 16 project follows the standard's post-implementation review. It aims to cut some ongoing application costs and clarify accounting for certain rent concessions. Scope and timing will come later.

The Board also agreed to begin the IFRS 17 post-implementation review in the first quarter of 2027, and split its IAS 38 intangibles review into two workstreams: disclosure improvements and a targeted look at recognition.
items.why: Crypto measurement and lease accounting are classic exam and thesis topics, and PSAK will follow these IFRS changes through DSAK IAI.

items.title: PCAOB splits enforcement into five specialist units, including one on AI
items.summary: The PCAOB restructured its Division of Enforcement and Investigations into five units on 10 November. One of them targets misconduct involving AI in public company audits.
detail: The new units are a Strategic Risk Unit (fraud and significant accounting issues), a Super Intelligence Unit (AI misuse in audits and AI tools for the Division), a Global Network Firm Unit for the largest firms, a Non-Affiliate Firm Unit for smaller practices, and an International Unit for cross-border cases.

The Global Network Firm Unit will focus on quality control and significant misconduct ahead of QC 1000, which takes effect on 15 December 2026. Debevoise notes the PCAOB's 2026 budget of $362.1 million is 9.4% below 2025.
items.why: It shows where US audit regulators expect risk to sit next, with AI use and firm-wide quality control at the top of the list.

items.title: PCAOB board considers 2026-2030 strategic plan and permanent broker-dealer inspections
items.summary: The PCAOB's 19 November open meeting was set to adopt its 2026-2030 strategic plan and FY2027 budget, and to propose a permanent inspection program for broker-dealer auditors.
detail: If approved, the 2027 budget goes to the SEC for sign-off, as the Sarbanes-Oxley Act requires.
The broker-dealer proposal would replace the interim inspection program that has run since 2011. The pre-meeting release does not report the outcome or budget figures.
items.why: Inspection regimes are the main lever regulators use to shape audit quality, a core theme in auditing units.

items.title: S&P 500 drops 3.7% as Nvidia slides 14%
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 3.70% on Friday 20 November to 6,910.39, its seventh straight loss and first close below 7,000 since 14 April. The index lost 8.61% over the week.
detail: Nvidia fell about 14% to $125.53 even after reporting Q3 revenue up 103% to $115.84 billion. Coverage pointed to China chip questions and leadership news at the company.

The Nasdaq Composite closed the week at 22,617.73, down 10.02%, and the Dow at 48,147.33, down 8.02%. The VIX ended at 35.89 after touching 40.03 on Friday. Hawkish FOMC minutes and bets on a December Fed hike added pressure, while the 10-year Treasury yield fell 24 bps on the week to 4.91%.
items.why: A sharp, concentrated sell-off in AI names is a live case study in market risk, concentration in index funds and impairment pressure on tech valuations.

items.title: Australian dollar hits 2026 low after 43,500 jobs lost in October
items.summary: AUD/USD fell through 0.6700 to just above 0.6650 after data showed Australia lost 43,500 jobs in October against a forecast gain of 25,000.
detail: Unemployment rose to 4.9% from 4.7%, its highest since late 2021. Part-time work made up 40,600 of the jobs lost.

The weak data lands weeks after the RBA lifted the cash rate to 4.85% on 3 November, while markets expect the Fed to raise rates on 9 December. The ASX 200 fell 1.6% on Friday to 8,593 and lost 5.4% for the week.
items.why: A weaker AUD changes the cost of studying and living in Melbourne in rupiah terms, and the jobs data complicates the RBA's next move.

items.title: Saudi Arabia confirms 15% domestic minimum top-up tax from 2027
items.summary: ZATCA announced on 19 November that a domestic minimum top-up tax will apply from 1 January 2027 to large multinational groups.
detail: The tax covers groups with consolidated revenue of €750 million or more in at least two of the four prior financial years. It applies when the effective tax rate on an entity's profits falls below 15%.
In a simplified example given by the authority, 9 million riyals of tax on 100 million riyals of profit leads to a top-up of about 6 million riyals. The full Pillar Two calculation is more detailed.
items.why: Another major economy adopting a QDMTT shows how Pillar Two keeps spreading even with US pushback on the global deal.

items.title: Australia publishes first 382 public country-by-country tax reports
items.summary: The ATO released the first tranche of public CbC reports, covering 201 Australian-headquartered and 181 foreign-headquartered groups.
detail: The reports show revenue, profit, income tax, employees and tangible assets for Australia and 40 specified jurisdictions, with other jurisdictions aggregated. The regime covers groups with global income of at least $1 billion and a sufficient Australian presence.
The data is on data.gov.au. This first tranche mainly covers groups with a 30 June year end, and more reports, many from foreign-headquartered groups, are expected in May 2027.
items.why: Public CbC data is new raw material for transfer pricing and profit-shifting research, right where you study.

items.title: Portugal's top tax court: missing TP filings do not remove the burden of proof
items.summary: Portugal's Supreme Administrative Court held that a taxpayer's failure to file transfer pricing disclosures does not free the tax authority from proving an arm's-length breach.
detail: The 4 November judgment granted the taxpayer's appeal against a lower court that had upheld extra corporate income tax assessments of €174,100 for 2007 and 2008.
The taxpayer was not named. The ruling confirms that the authority must still show the controlled transaction departed from arm's-length terms before adjusting.
items.why: Burden of proof is central in TP disputes, and the same question comes up often at Indonesia's Pengadilan Pajak.

items.title: EU scraps €150 VAT threshold; France rejects 2027 Finance Bill
items.summary: The EU Council approved removing the €150 threshold for the deemed supplier rule and import one-stop shop from 1 July 2028, and France's lower house rejected the 2027 Finance Bill.
detail: The French bill included a proposed change to the Pillar Two threshold, which falls with it for now.
Kenya extended its initial minimum top-up tax notification deadline to 30 November 2026, and Poland's upper house passed a corporate income tax rate increase.
items.why: It is a quick view of how Pillar Two and e-commerce VAT rules are shifting country by country.

items.title: Digital economy tax hits Rp14.07 trillion in January to October 2026
items.summary: DJP collected Rp14.07 trillion from the digital economy in the first ten months of 2026, bringing the cumulative total to Rp60.1 trillion by 31 October.
detail: The 2026 figure breaks down into PPN PMSE Rp10.69 trillion, SIPP procurement Rp1.95 trillion, fintech Rp1.09 trillion and crypto Rp341.61 billion. PPN PMSE for all of 2025 was Rp10.32 trillion.
DJP has designated 280 PMSE VAT collectors, of which 249 have collected and remitted. No new collectors were added in January to October 2026.
items.why: Indonesia's VAT on foreign digital suppliers is a working example of the destination-based approach the OECD promotes.

items.title: Crypto tax receipts reach Rp2.23 trillion since 2022
items.summary: Cumulative crypto tax reached Rp2.23 trillion by October 2026, made up of PPh 22 of Rp1.34 trillion and domestic VAT of Rp881.82 billion.
detail: Annual receipts were Rp246.54 billion in 2022, Rp220.89 billion in 2023, Rp620.38 billion in 2024 and Rp796.74 billion in 2025. January to October 2026 brought Rp341.61 billion.
items.why: Crypto taxation links directly to the new IASB project on how cryptoassets should be measured.

items.title: IHSG loses 3.71% in a week of BI hike and foreign selling
items.summary: The IHSG closed the week of 16 to 20 November at 5,146.326, down 3.71%, after Bank Indonesia raised the BI-Rate 25 bps to 6%.
detail: Market capitalisation fell 3.56% to Rp8,725 trillion, and foreign investors net sold Rp947.41 billion on Friday alone. Average daily value fell 47.9% to Rp12.347 trillion.
BI says the rupiah has weakened 8.47% so far in 2026. It closed at Rp18,255 per USD on Thursday 19 November.
items.why: A rate hike to defend the rupiah while stocks fall shows the policy trade-offs of an emerging market under capital outflow.

items.title: Kemenkeu needs about Rp514 trillion in tax in November and December
items.summary: The Ministry of Finance estimates it needs Rp590.1 trillion of revenue in the last two months of 2026, around Rp514 trillion of it from taxes.
detail: Hitting the 2026 tax target requires roughly 23% growth on last year. A CORE economist expects the 2026 budget deficit at about 2.8% to 2.9% of GDP.
items.why: A large year-end shortfall usually means more SP2DK letters and audits, which feeds directly into tax disputes.

worth.title: Australia publishes first 382 public country-by-country tax reports
worth.text: Australia's public CbC regime is now live, giving anyone jurisdiction-level data on revenue, profit and tax paid by large multinationals. It is a ready-made dataset for a transfer pricing or BEPS assignment.
